bradesco.structure: Habitat model — open co-innovation space (Inovabra) + internal R&D + corporate venture (via acquisitions like Digio)

signal_to_scale.mechanism: Inovabra habitat curation; startups must have mature product
Internal tech teams; BTRL-like readiness evaluation (not publicly formalized as 'BTRL' in this round — OPEN_QUESTION)
Bridge sandbox for GenAI use cases; internal experimentation
BIA evolution; Bridge 500+ use cases (70 at scale)
Bridge centralized platform; BIA at 24M users

bradesco.governance: CTO-led (Cíntia Scovine); centralized GenAI guardrails via Bridge; multicloud strategy
bradesco.universities: Not researched in depth in this round — PendingRecord
bradesco.radar_history_note: Bradesco does not publicly publish a formal 'Technology Radar' in the ThoughtWorks sense; maturity is inferred from executive disclosures. See technology-radar-history.json for reconstructed versions.

credicorp_bcp.structure: Portfolio model — disruptive initiatives managed as a VC-like portfolio (Yape, Tenpo, Culqi, iO) + Krealo corporate venture fund + BCP Xplore Open Banking unit

signal_to_scale.mechanism: Krealo scouting; BCP Xplore API ecosystem
Internal product teams for each initiative
Yape reached profitability ahead of projection
Yape at scale; BCP Xplore APIs in production
Target: 10% of risk-adjusted group revenue from disruptive initiatives by 2026

credicorp_bcp.governance: Portfolio-level metrics (contribution to group revenue); each initiative has own P&L
credicorp_bcp.key_difference: Credicorp communicates innovation as financial contribution to group revenue; Bradesco communicates as use-case counts and tech investment — different languages, not directly comparable.

comparison_note: Inovabra (open habitat, physical co-innovation) vs Credicorp disruptive-portfolio (internal ventures with revenue targets) are structurally different instruments. Comparing them as 'which is better at innovation' is a category error without first agreeing on the metric (network breadth vs portfolio ROI).
